• Follow I‑278 W until you reach the interchange with **I‑95 N** (the New England Thruway). | The 5th Avenue Bridge is usually less congested than the Brooklyn Bridge during peak hours. | | **2. I‑95 N to Boston** | • Stay on **I‑95 N** for the entire stretch.

• Take the appropriate exit for your destination in Boston (e.g., **Exit 1** for downtown, **Exit 2** for the North End, etc.). | I‑95 N is the most direct corridor between NYC and Boston. It’s a toll road in Connecticut and Massachusetts, so have an E‑ZPass or cash ready. | | **3. Into Boston** | • After exiting I‑95, follow local streets to your final address. | Use a navigation app (Google Maps, Waze, Apple Maps) for real‑time traffic updates and lane‑by‑lane guidance. | ### Quick Tips 1. **Check Traffic** – Peak commute times (Mon‑Fri 7–9 am & 4–6 pm) can add 30–60 min. 2. **Tolls** – Connecticut and Massachusetts have tolls on I‑95/I‑90. Enjoy your trip! 🚗💨
